text:
incident-bot: Pager: elevated p50/p99 latency on streaming endpoints in us-west-2. Error spike around token flush path. Auto-escalation -> @alex oncall

alex: got it, looking. seeing increased queue depth on stream-proxy and many half-open tls conns.

maria: I can pull logs + flamegraphs, sending query now.

sam: @alex do we have a quick mitigation? customers are seeing timeouts on streaming sessions.

alex: short-term: want to gate new streaming sessions + reduce concurrency per-worker. prefer non-intrusive first (rate limit new streams) then consider disabling streaming for lower tiers if needed.

rebecca: heads-up from support: 3 active enterprise customers reported degraded UX (stream pauses) and one has an open high-severity ticket. They want ETA.

kai: agree with gating. can we flip a feature-flag to disable streaming at the proxy layer per-customer?

alex: yes. we have a runtime flag `streaming.enabled` with per-tenant override. plan: 1) globally throttle new streaming handshake to 5r/s 2) for non-paid/standard tiers set `streaming.enabled=false` 3) route existing streaming sessions to a reduced chunk size (to ease memory).

maria: running the queries now. early signs point to a mem leak in the chunk-assembler when streaming chunk size > 4k. lowering chunk size will reduce allocation spikes.

product-bot: Note: disabling streaming will affect client UX (no progressive tokens). We should post a banner and update telemetry to mark impacted sessions.

alex: agreed. @support-led can you prep a short customer message: "We're throttling streaming while we stabilize latency. Responses will still be returned but may be delivered at once rather than streamed."

support-led: drafting, will share in 10m.

sam: operational steps?

alex: I will:
- patch proxy config to set new-session throttle to 5/s: `curl -XPOST https://ops-api/configs/stream-proxy -d '{\"new_stream_qps\":5}'`
- flip tenant override for `tier:standard` to `streaming.enabled=false` via admin UI
- deploy runtime change to reduce chunk size: `STREAM_CHUNK_MAX=2048` to all stream workers (can roll via canary)

maria: I have the flamegraphs and heap diffs, pushing to the incident channel. Looks like chunk buffer allocation spikes correlate with p99s.

kai: I'll prepare the infra job to apply the chunk size change across the fleet with a 10% canary.

alex: doing the throttle config now.

[system] config-update-bot: applied config `stream-proxy:new_stream_qps=5` (change id cfg-2026-7882)

alex: throttle applied. watching metrics. p50 dropped immediately, p99 still elevated but trending down.

maria: starting canary for chunk size change on 10% stream workers.

sam: any noticeable customer errors?

support-led: customers see fewer timeouts. still a couple of pause reports. status update drafted, tagging affected accounts.

[system] canary-deploy-bot: START canary deploy STREAM_CHUNK_MAX=2048 on stream-workers group a (10%)

maria: canary looks healthy for 12m, memory allocations down ~30%. p99 for canary nodes back to baseline.

kai: scheduling progressive rollout: 10% every 5 minutes, will pause on error.

alex: while rollout proceeds, set tenant overrides for standard tier -> disable streaming. doing admin change now.

[system] admin-bot: tenant-override applied: `tier:standard` streaming.enabled=false (change id to-345)
